messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@orbitpay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in failures / long tail during peak window

Hi Mina,

We're seeing sustained error rate spikes (5xx) during our US evening peak over the last 3 days. P95 looks fine but P99/P999 jumps and completions stall — the UX times out and we get a handful of successful completions but many failures. Impact: checkout failures for ~6% of sessions during 17:00-18:30 PST yesterday.

Attached are a trace dump and p99 CSV slices. Highlights:
- 17:12:34 — a cluster of requests show sequencing lengths beyond our usual (avg tokens ~230 -> spikes to 900).
- Several requests show repeated retries and then 502 responses.

This is urgent for us. We rely on predictable tails during flash promotions. Can/from you confirm: did you change concurrency caps or routing for our dedicated pool this week? Any guidance or temporary mitigations we can apply on our side?

We need a bridge if possible — Natalie (CTO) is CC'd.

Thanks,
Alex
OrbitPay — Head of Integrations

Attachments: orbitpay-traces-0423.log (log snippet), orbitpay-p99-metrics-20270423.csv (metrics)

Subject: OrbitPay: p99/p999 surge — triage + immediate mitigations

Team — forwarding OrbitPay's traces (attached). Customer reports: 6% checkout failures during US evening peak; sequences sometimes spike to ~900 tokens. They are on a dedicated pool (Pool-ID OP-ded-7).

Please confirm within 30 minutes:
- Is OP-ded-7 showing concurrency cap saturation or rejection counts?
- Evidence of KV cache eviction churn for large prefix variance?
- Any abnormal kernel OOMs / GPU throttling spikes around 17:00 PST on 4/22 and 4/23?

If we see cap saturation, please propose an immediate action plan (short-term mitigation and conservative rollback plan): e.g. temp cap increase + selective routing to warmed fallback variant + enable aggressive KV prefix caching for high-frequency flows.

We may need to request exec visibility (Markus) if this requires credits or wholesale routing changes. Customer is sensitive (flash promo this week).

Mina

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitPay: p99/p999 surge — triage + immediate mitigations

Quick triage notes (initial):
- OP-ded-7 is reporting request rejections hitting the concurrency cap between 17:05-17:35 PST for both 4/22 and 4/23. Rejection count ~480 over the 90min window.
- KV cache churn is high: high sequence-length variance causes very low prefix reuse; LRU eviction rate spiked ~4x. This results in heavier compute per request.
- No GPU OOMs, but per-token latency increased due to longer effective sequences; some requests retried by client and then hit throttle -> 502/503 pattern.

Immediate mitigations we can kick off (I can run these now, request your sign-off Mina):
1) Temporarily bump concurrency cap for OP-ded-7 from 120->180 for next 3 hours, closely monitor rejections and GPU utilization. (Risk: increased contention elsewhere on that host pool; we'll route only their pool traffic.)
2) Activate a warmed fallback variant (quantized model variant with slightly lower context handling) and route 10% of their traffic during the peak window. This reduces cost but improves tail success.
3) Enable aggressive KV prefix retention for keys matching OrbitPay request signatures (short-term TTL extension).
4) Add soft-client-side guidance: reduce client retries to avoid exacerbating retry storm. Mina, recommend you ask them to cut retries to 1 for the next 2 hours.

I'll prepare dashboards for the bridge and a short rollback plan.

— Dylan
Senior SRE (Inference)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@orbitpay.com>, Natalie Park <natalie@orbitpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary & next steps — OrbitPay impact window (consumer promo)

Markus — quick executive note and ask for visibility. OrbitPay experienced persistent p99/p999 tail failures during their evening promo window 4/22-4/23. Impact: ~6% checkout failure during 17:00-18:30 PST; customer is asking for a remediation timeline and potential credits.

What we did:
- SRE actions (Dylan): temporary concurrency cap increase (120->180) for OP-ded-7, deployed warmed quantized fallback for 10% of traffic, increased KV prefix TTL for OrbitPay signatures. Immediate effect: error rate dropped from ~6% -> ~1.4% within 20 minutes during the re-test window.
- Root contributors: sequence-length variance causing KV cache churn + concurrency cap rejections compounded by client-side retries. No platform-wide kernel or OOM faults found.

Customer impact & ask: OrbitPay wants an exec touchpoint and a goodwill credit to offset revenue lost during the promo. Suggested options:
- Offer 10% credit for April bill or a one-time service credit tied to April usage; OR
- Provide technical follow-up: a short-term traffic optimization plan + 2-week partnership engagement to tune their prompt shaping and caching keys (Redwood Optimize engagement).

Recommendation: please greenlight a one-time 10% credit contingent on a 2-week joint optimization workshop (SRE + Solutions). If approved, I'll confirm on the 17:00 PST bridge tomorrow and coordinate the customer-facing message.

Alex/Natalie — we have a remediation path and saw measurable improvement after the mitigations. Can you confirm whether reduced client retries (to 1) is feasible for the promo tail period? We'll hold the increased cap for another 24 hours while we validate.

Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-mitigation-checklist.pdf; orbitpay-traces-0423.log; drive link to full traces: https://drive.redwood/inflight/op_logs/orbitpay/0423
